about: The explainer's narration, one line per step. `say`, where given, is what the voice says instead of `text` (numbers written for speaking). narrate.py voices them into audio/step-N.mp3, which the explainer plays when its sound is on.

lines.text: stretto-proxy wraps any MCP server. The host runs it in place of the server's command, and it forwards every message both ways, unchanged. The agent keeps its prompt and its tools. Until you give the proxy a flow, it only forwards and records.

Use the agent as usual. The proxy writes each session to a log: the calls, their results, and the conversation if the host shares it. The logs are all a flow learns from, so record the kinds of request the agent will see. In replay, ten of an agent's own sessions gave over 90% of what all of them did.

lines.text: stretto learn counts which reads followed which calls, and where each read's arguments came from: here, the order numbers in the user's record. The result is a flow, a file you review like code, with flow-show and flow-diff.

Served, the flow runs after each of the agent's calls. It makes the lookups the agent is likely to need, with arguments bound from the results so far, and they ride in the same tool result. The agent has them before it would ask, so it spends fewer LLM turns. Run a flow in shadow first, then promote the sites whose lookups were the agent's own.

A detour is a lookup the agent did not use. Its result stays in the context, so every later LLM turn reads it again: that is its cost, in tokens. It cannot change the state, since a flow only reads. Live, a detour carried about 2,530 input tokens, and a saved turn saved about 6,000.
lines.say: A detour is a lookup the agent did not use. Its result stays in the context, so every later LLM turn reads it again: that is its cost, in tokens. It cannot change the state, since a flow only reads. Live, a detour carried about twenty-five hundred input tokens, and a saved turn saved about six thousand.

lines.text: The reach decider asks no model and needs no key. It makes a lookup when the chance that the agent uses it before its next write clears a threshold set by those costs, about 0.3. That chance, not the chance the read comes next, is the one that pays: the agent may reply first, and still read it before it writes.

Live, on 28 τ²-bench retail and airline tasks, stretto cut Claude Sonnet 5's LLM turns by 20.5%, Claude Haiku 4.5's by 22.4%, and GLM-5.3's by 27.9%. The savings are in retail; in airline they are not established. Asking the agent to batch its reads saved 3 to 8%, and with that prompt in place, stretto still saved 17 to 23% more. In AgentDojo's Slack and travel suites, turns fell 10.1%; in BFCL there was no effect.
lines.say: Live, on twenty-eight tau two bench retail and airline tasks, stretto cut Claude Sonnet five's L L M turns by twenty point five percent, Claude Haiku four point five's by twenty-two point four, and G L M five point three's by twenty-seven point nine. The savings are in retail; in airline they are not established. Asking the agent to batch its reads saved three to eight percent, and with that prompt in place, stretto still saved seventeen to twenty-three percent more. In Agent Dojo's Slack and travel suites, turns fell ten percent; in B F C L there was no effect.
